question: Timolol eye drops are contraindicated in patients with asthma or COPD because sufficient drug is absorbed systemically via the nasolacrimal duct to cause clinically significant bronchoconstriction.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true and is clinically very important. Topical timolol can cause significant systemic beta-blockade via nasolacrimal absorption. Patients with asthma, COPD, heart block, or severe bradycardia should avoid ocular beta-blockers. Use prostaglandin analogues or carbonic anhydrase inhibitors instead.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Approximately 80% of a topical eye drop drains through the nasolacrimal duct into the nasal mucosa and GI tract, bypassing first-pass metabolism. Timolol is a non-selective beta-blocker; systemic absorption can cause bronchoconstriction in susceptible patients. Punctal occlusion for 1–2 minutes after instillation reduces systemic absorption by ~40%.
